correctness.rationale: After monomial normalization of a weight-\(w\) center, the distance to a representative is exactly \(b+w-\max(a_1,\ldots,a_{q-1})\). The two independent choice counts are the outside-support binomial factor and the support multinomial factor. Removing the unique zero vector and dividing every remaining scalar orbit by \(q-1\) yields the enumerator. The orbit statement follows because monomial isometries are transitive on each weight class and shell profiles distinguish different weights. Exact exhaustive replay agrees for every center weight for \(q\in\{2,3,4,5\}\), \(1\le n\le4\), including the non-prime field \(\mathbb F_4\).

value.rationale: Exact ball volumes are a first-order invariant for sphere-packing, covering, random-received-word, and decoding analyses of a newly proposed coding metric. The result is all-parameter rather than a small census and also reveals a structural obstruction to treating this projective metric as homogeneous: its full isometry orbits are exactly the Hamming-weight classes. This is materially stronger than merely evaluating the pointwise distance algorithm on examples.
